finding: An MCP initialize with the clientInfo key removed answers HTTP 500 with a plain-text, non-JSON-RPC body naming an internal .NET type: "JSON deserialization for type 'ModelContextProtocol.Protocol.InitializeRequestParams' was missing required properties including: 'clientInfo'." Refusing the request is correct, because the MCP specification requires clientInfo. The finding is the shape: the same server answers an unknown tool name with a proper JSON-RPC -32602 inside a 200, so it has an error channel and reaches for a 500 here instead. A client that omits clientInfo, or whose library omits it, gets a server-fault status and a string it cannot parse as a protocol error, and the string tells it the name of a class rather than what to fix.

reproducibility.command: curl -si -X POST https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{}}}'
